articles.title: Black Friday is about to deliver a reality check to the retail bears
articles.summary: The US consumer is looking surprisingly strong at the start of the holiday shopping season.
articles.body:
The holiday season officially kicks off today, giving investors a break from all things Nvidia ( NVDA ) and reinstated CEO Jensen Huang.

Thanksgiving Day deal shopping after consuming your turkey begins this afternoon. Black Friday is coming tomorrow.

And despite all the noise about inflation, interest rates, and consumer anxiety, there are reasons to believe retailers could have a very strong holiday season, and their stock prices could perform well into year-end.

1. Retailers are already showing signs of life

Target just delivered a strong third quarter. Sales climbed 7.1%. Comparable sales increased 5.6%. And store traffic was up 5%.

More people are walking into Target despite gas over $4 a gallon. They're buying more merchandise. And digital sales are growing, too.

"At the start of the year we were laser focused on what our strategy needed to be, and it's getting back to the unique lane that we play in retail, and that's always going to be a combination of leading with style and design, and of course, incredible value," Target CEO Michael Fiddelke told Yahoo Finance . "The 'I can't believe the quality of this,' or 'I can't believe I found it at Target at a price point' that makes the smile get wider. Once someone turns over the price tag, that's when we're at our best, and then you add to that, continuing to make the experience even better and more consistent. Like that's been the work we're doing, and in the categories where we've leaned in most to drive change, we really like the response we're seeing."

That's not a consumer who has completely shut down.

Target also raised its full-year sales growth outlook to around 6%.

The stock is hovering around a 52-week high, up 79% on the year.

And it's not just about Target. We're seeing retailers such as Walmart ( WMT ) fight aggressively for consumer dollars with better assortments, compelling prices, and more reasons to shop. They are winning, as underscored by Walmart CFO John David Rainey, who said on Sozzi Unleashed that the holidays have started well.

Best Buy ( BBY ) is also in the winning column — it just reported its best sales growth in years this week.

The key takeaway: Retailers are entering the holiday season with some real momentum.

2. The US consumer still has money to spend

The consumer remains a major engine of the US economy. Household finances have held up despite major inflationary pressure, income growth is providing support, and rising stock and home values have helped many households feel wealthier.

articles.title: Man booked Rs 86 lakh flat, paid Rs 14.76 lakh and Rs 25.05 lakh in EMIs as construction stalled; District Commission ordered refund with 9% interest, EMI reimbursement, loan settlement, but State Commission rejects plea for more relief
articles.summary: You book a flat and pay a booking amount while also getting a home loan to finance the remaining payment.
articles.body: You book a flat and pay a booking amount while also getting a home loan to finance the remaining payment. However after a few years you discover that the project has allegedly been abandoned by the developer. What do you do?In one such case, the District Consumer Commission ordered the real estate developer to refund the homebuyer’s booking amount, reimburse earlier EMIs and settle the loan liability.What the case is aboutA homebuyer booked a 237-square-yard residential floor in a real estate project in Sonipat in February 2017. He paid Rs 14.76 lakh towards the property and also got a home loan.According to his complaint, the possession was promised by October 2019. However, the homebuyer alleged that when he visited the construction site in December 2019, work had stopped and he learnt that the project had been abandoned.He also alleged that the finance company had disbursed Rs 67,47,091 directly to the developer without verifying the construction stage.The homebuyer said he had paid Rs 25,05,615 in EMIs and sent a legal notice in January 2020 seeking cancellation of the allotment. He relied on the tripartite agreement, arguing that the developer was responsible for repaying the loan to the finance company and returning his contribution, subject to applicable administrative charges.The real estate developer contested the complaint. It claimed that possession for fit-out purposes had been offered through a letter in August 2018, and that the homebuyer had outstanding dues. It also challenged the complaint on limitation, jurisdiction and consumer-status grounds, alleging that the property had been booked for commercial purposes. The finance company maintained that the homebuyer obligation to repay the loan continued independently of the dispute with the developer.The District Commission rejected the developer's force majeure defence, noting that it had not produced evidence to establish that the delay resulted from circumstances beyond its control.It observed: "admittedly, there is inordinate delay in handing over the possession of the flat in question which amounts to deficiency in service."The commission also found that the developer had not established that the homebuyer was dealing in real estate for commercial purposes. It held both respondents guilty of deficiency in service.The District Commission directed the real estate to refund Rs 14.76 lakh with interest at 9% per annum from the respective dates of deposit. If the refund was not made within four weeks of receipt of the order, the interest rate would rise to 12% per annum until realisation. It also awarded Rs 1 lakh for mental agony and harassment and Rs 25,000 towards litigation costs.Separately, the developer was directed to pay the loan amount to the finance company, reimburse the EMIs paid from May 2017 to September 2020 with interest at 9% from the date of each payment, and settle the future EMI and loan liability with the lender.Why District Consumer Commission ruled in favour of homebuyer and State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission dismissed later pleaHowever, the homebuyer appealed because he wanted reimbursement extended to the installments paid during the complaint proceedings. He sought reimbursement of EMIs paid up to May 2024, which he quantified at Rs 60,56,700. He also asked for litigation costs to be increased from Rs 25,000 to Rs 5 lakh.The State Commission noted that the finance company had not appealed against the District Commission's order, which had therefore attained finality in relation to that respondent.It also rejected the lender's limitation objection because the homebuyer’s application seeking condonation of delay in filing the appeal had already been allowed. Since the homebuyer’s principal grievance concerned the developer, the commission said it would not discuss the finance company's other submissions in the appeal.The central question was whether the District Commission's order needed modification. The State Commission examined the existing directions on reimbursement and the future loan liability.It explained: "A perusal of the above referred clause (ii) makes it clear that District Commission has not only directed OP1 to pay the EMI amount to OP 2 from May 2017 to Sept 2020, but also directed OP1 to settle the future EMI/loan amount with OP2."The commission considered this direction sufficient to address the homebuyer’s grievance.It stated: "Since Ld. District Commission has already directed respondent1 to settle the future EMI/Loan amount with respondent no 2, we are of the considered view that the grievance of appellant has already been taken care of by Ld. District Commission."It therefore rejected the argument that the District Commission had failed to provide for the loan liability during the complaint proceedings. It also found no grounds to increase litigation costs to Rs 5 lakh.Concluding that the original order required no modification, the State Commission observed: "Thus, in view of above discussion we find no infirmity and illegality in the impugned order passed by the Ld. District Forum which needs modification by this Commission."The appeal was dismissed, with both sides directed to bear their own costs. The original relief remained in place, but the homebuyer did not obtain the additional modification he sought.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Wall Street is in chaos. Don't let it ruin your Thanksgiving.
articles.summary: A few Thanksgiving Day investing reminders.
articles.body:
Thanksgiving has arrived. And with it, the official start of the holiday season.

I know a lot of you are going to sit down with your families today, carve up the inflationary turkey, have a few stiff drinks, and probably check your portfolios somewhere between the mashed potatoes and protein-packed dessert.

And I will say this: What a week to be an investor — whether casual or hardcore active trader.

We've had a massive market sell-off. We've watched Nvidia's ( NVDA ) super-important stock swing wildly in price. We've seen Jensen Huang return to the CEO chair and remind everybody just how much influence one person can have over this market, if not the entire world.

I want to serve up a few things to consider.

First, don't confuse a bad week in the market with a bad investment strategy. Markets go up. Markets go down. Your job isn't to react to every headline. It's to know what you own and why you own it.

Use this time to reconnect with what you own and why. If those theses have been blown up, acknowledge it and take action.

Second, don't fall in love with a stock. Not Nvidia, with its no-succession-plan-loving leader back at the helm. Not any company. Great businesses can be terrible investments at the wrong price. And no CEO, no matter how brilliant, is bigger than the fundamentals.

Thank you, HPE CEO Antonio Neri, for reminding me of that this week .

Third, remember that volatility is part of the deal in investing. If you want the long-term rewards of investing, you have to be willing to live through the uncomfortable days like we are seeing right now. Sometimes the hardest thing to do is absolutely nothing.

And finally, don't forget what all this investing is supposed to be for.

It's supposed to help you build a better life. More freedom. More opportunity. More time with the people who actually matter in your life (and that's not Jensen Huang).

Not another reason to stare at your iPhone Duo while your family is sitting across the table.

To everyone who watches Yahoo Finance, reads our stories, challenges us, agrees with us, disagrees with us — thank you. Seriously. We don't take your time or your trust for granted.

I'm grateful you're riding with me. I'm grateful we get to do this every day. And I'm grateful to be part of your financial journey.

Enjoy the turkey. Hug your family. Dress up your pet in a cute holiday costume. Call somebody you haven't spoken to in a while. If you have investing questions, get at me on X @BrianSozzi — I will obviously be online waiting for the next Jensen headline.

articles.title: Higher borrowing costs weigh on G4 economies, cloud 2027 rate hike outlook: Report
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Higher borrowing costs are beginning to weigh more heavily on business demand across major developed economies, potentially reducing the need
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Higher borrowing costs are beginning to weigh more heavily on business demand across major developed economies, potentially reducing the need for further interest rate increases in 2027, even as central banks are widely expected to raise rates by 25 basis points each in December, according to a report by S&P Global.Business activity growth across the US, UK, Japan and the eurozone slowed for a second consecutive month in November, hitting its weakest level since June, as elevated prices, economic uncertainty and higher borrowing costs continued to constrain demand.The latest purchasing managers' index (PMI) data showed that businesses were increasingly reporting weaker sales due to rising borrowing costs, ahead of the anticipated rate hikes next month."If sustained, the demand slowdown could potentially limit the need for further increases into 2027," S&P Global said, as quoted by ANI.The report noted that while all four major central banks are expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points in December, the outlook for further tightening next year remains uncertain."There is less certainty over the extent to which rates will need to rise further in 2027, with all the major central banks data dependent," it said.Lower global crude oil prices provided some relief on the inflation front in November, easing price pressures across all four economies. However, selling price inflation remained among the highest levels recorded over the past three years, indicating that cost pressures had not fully subsided.Higher costs also affected labour market conditions, with employment growth slowing in the US, while the UK and eurozone reported job losses. S&P Global said policymakers would closely track business output, new orders and employment trends to assess companies' pricing power and workers' ability to negotiate higher wages."November’s PMI data already saw increased reporting by companies of the demand dampening impact of higher borrowing costs," the report said.Central banks across major economies have been pursuing monetary tightening to contain inflation. The European Central Bank has raised rates twice by 25 basis points each this year, while the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England have each delivered a 25-basis-point hike. The Bank of Japan has also continued its longer-term monetary tightening cycle.In India, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has also been adjusting its monetary policy in response to inflation and growth conditions, with its rate decisions closely watched for their impact on borrowing costs, credit demand and economic activity.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Yasir Al-Rumayyan explaining why Saudi Arabia PIF bought Newcastle United
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia PIF Governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan flew in for the Newcastle United match against Arsenal. He didn’t pick a bad one.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia PIF Governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan flew in for the Newcastle United match against Arsenal.

As always though, when Yasir Al-Rumayyan is part of a PIF visiting group to Tyneside, it also sparks intrigue as to other potential reasons for his/their visit.

On Wednesday, an exclusive from The Athletic reported that the Newcastle United owners were now planning to sell a stake in the club that would enable a new party (or parties) to own 25% of NUFC.

The report stating that this would be done by issuing new shares.

So if a 25% share in the club was sold via the issue of new shares, the Saudi Arabia PIF and the Reuben family (Chris Waugh at The Athletic has on Thursday confirmed that they as well as PIF would see their shareholding diluted) would see their ownership of the club reduce respectively from 84% to 63% and 16% to 12%.

The Athletic reporting on Wednesday that the idea with selling the 25% stake in NUFC is not for any money to go directly to PIF or the Reubens, instead it is intended that the money generated by selling a quarter ownership of the club would be put towards spending on the infrastructure, the state of the art training ground and a new stadium. With estimates of a club current valuation now of up to £2billion, that would potentially mean up to £500million raised towards financing the new Newcastle United stadium and training ground.

Unsurprisingly this sparked a lot of conjecture in the media and amongst fans.

Was the Yasir Al-Rumayyan visit to Tyneside not simply to watch the Arsenal match and indeed, what did The Athletic exclusive potentially suggest about future plans of the Saudi Arabia PIF majority ownership?

I think what is key is to go back and revisit exactly why PIF bought a controlling stake in Newcastle United.

This below is Yasir Al-Rumayyan handily explaining himself why the Saudi Arabia PIF bought the majority ownership of the club.

Yasir Al-Rumayyan speaking on 4 October 2022, a few days before the first anniversary of the Newcastle United takeover:

"We bought the whole team (Newcastle United) for £350m, instead of only having 30 per cent in another team (Manchester United) for £700m.

"You can see Chelsea was sold for $3.5bn (£2.5bn).

"So, my potential now is to go from £350m to at least $3.5bn (£2.5bn).

"Football of course is one of the most important sports there is, whether domestically (in Saudi Arabia) or abroad.

"It is the number one sport in the world and why the English Premier League?

"Well, because it is the best league in the world, no other league competes with it.

"There are 20 teams, three are relegated, three are promoted, the advantage of the Premier League is that any of the 20 teams can beat the best team in the league.

"When we looked at it, we looked at it from a financial perspective.

"By the way, it wasn't the first offer we got regarding a football team. We looked in Italy, France and the UK as well.

"In the UK there was a team (Manchester United) that approached us on the basis that we take 30 per cent of the ownership and (on the condition that) we don't interfere at all in terms of managing the club, for £700m.

"Then we bought Newcastle, who offered us 100 per cent of the ownership, but Amanda Staveley and her husband who got us the opportunity told us, 'We like it so much, we would like to be with you'….and that was perfect.

"Then came the Reuben family, who are one of the biggest property investors (in the UK), saying that, 'We would like to come with you', and these are one of the biggest investors in (the City of) Newcastle (Upon Tyne).

"I said, 'Perfect! Tell them to come'. So now they (Amanda Staveley, her husband and the Reubens) have a skin in the game."

Just under five months later, Amanda Staveley was speaking at the FT Business of Football Summit in Mayfair, London on Thursday 2 March 2023 and she then gave further insight into why the Saudi Arabia PIF had decided to buy Newcastle United:

"When we walked into a Newcastle United game we said why spend X Billion when you can spend three hundred and some million and put in….I think we have put in two hundred plus to date of new money since we bought the club.

"We had a particular business plan, based on a five, ten, fifteen year timeline.

"Critical to that plan was making sure we had the right partners.

"So making sure (Saudi Arabia) PIF, who are very long-term investors.

"Hoping potentially there might be the chance of Champions League.

"I love the valuations that are reflecting in Chelsea….because it makes our valuation look very compelling.

"We bought the club at under two times revenue.

"When you are looking at five to seven times revenue, that is a lot of money."

What was said by Yasir Al-Rumayyan just over four years ago (and then Amanda Staveley just over three and a half years ago) very much fits in with what is happening now, in my opinion. Their prediction/expectation of huge growth in the value of Newcastle United has become reality and now further steps to be taken in order to help push that valuation far far higher. Part of that plan appears to now be to bring in money from other investors which will help to finance essential infrastructure projects, namely the stadium and training ground. Injecting cash from elsewhere via an issue of new shares that then reduces the levels of money that may then needed to be loaned to help cover the spending, plus it also reduces the exposure of the Saudi Arabia PIF and the Reubens.

articles.title: Lazio Bracing Themselves for Inevitable January Transfer Ban
articles.summary: While the official confirmation won’t arrive until December, Lazio reportedly realise they won’t be allowed to operate in the market in January.Lazio Have Be...
articles.body:
While the official confirmation won't arrive until December, Lazio reportedly realise they won't be allowed to operate in the market in January.

Lazio Have Been Struggling to Keep Their Market Open

Against all odds, the Aquile currently lead the Serie A standings. However, their balance sheet paints a less bright picture of the club's general status. In the summer of 2025, Lazio were infamously banned from any transfer activities after failing to meet the required financial standards.

Claudio Lotito and Angelo Fabiani (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)

Last January, the club sold Taty Castellanos and Matteo Guendouzi, earning enough capital gains to prevent another summer ban. However, the Biancocelesti still failed to meet the required Squad Cost Ratio threshold of 0.7, so they were forced to operate under net-zero restrictions in the summer of 2026, meaning they could only sign new players using freshly generated transfer funds.

Rating Lazio 2026 Summer Transfer Campaign: The Zero-Cost Masterclass

Luckily for Lazio, Sporting Director Angelo Fabiani was able to deliver despite the restrictions, recruiting the likes of Davide Frattesi, Josip Sutalo, and Albert Gudmundsson. The club also sold Mario Gila, Alessio Romagnoli, and Ivan Provedel, but it wasn't necessarily sufficient to balance the books.

According to Il Messaggero (via La Lazio Siamo Noi ), Fabiani and Lazio president Claudio Lotito are both aware that a transfer ban in January is considered almost inevitable. By the end of November, the club must present its financial statements to the supervisory committee, which then hands down its verdict in December.

Claudio Lotito (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)

While it was recently suggested that Lotito could try to plug the deficit by deferring taxes or collecting sponsorship money in advance, the hierarchy believes these figures won't be sufficient to settle the situation. Therefore, the hierarchy has seemingly accepted the outcome.

Why Lazio Aren't Keen on Net-Zero Market

The Roman newspaper adds that the best Lazio could hope for at the moment is another net-zero market, but Lotito and Fabiani aren't too enticed by this possibility. After all, they would only be able to sign new players by offloading some of their own, whereas they had already promised Gennaro Gattuso they wouldn't cash in on any important players in the middle of the season.
